evidence.claim: Joshua trees and steel arches mark a highway across two deserts.
evidence.quote: the southern segment runs through a vast array of Joshua trees and the ecological boundaries of the Mohave and Sonoran Deserts.

evidence.claim: steel arches
evidence.quote: crosses Burro Creek over dual steel arch bridges

evidence.claim: Joshua Forest Scenic Road follows US 93 through Joshua trees at the ecological boundaries of the Mohave and Sonoran deserts.
evidence.quote: the southern segment runs through a vast array of Joshua trees and the ecological boundaries of the Mohave and Sonoran Deserts.

evidence.claim: ADOT credits this scenery with earning 54 miles of the highway between Wikieup and Wickenburg scenic-road recognition in 1993.
evidence.quote: The unusual scenery along 54 miles of U.S. 93 between Wickieup and Wickenburg earned it recognition as the Joshua Forest Scenic Road in 1993.

evidence.claim: The larger Wickenburg-to-I-40 highway combines divided sections with narrow two-lane stretches undergoing widening.
evidence.quote: While most of US 93 is a four-lane divided highway, sections of the highway between Wickenburg and I-40 are still narrow two-lane roads, gradually being upgraded to match the rest of the route.

evidence.claim: Its route was contested before it carried the US 93 number.
evidence.quote: This proposal was protested by the towns of Aguila and Wickenburg that argued that US 93 should pass through their towns rather than the proposed alignment to the east.

evidence.claim: In 1935, Aguila and Wickenburg opposed a proposed extension through Ash Fork; Wickenburg argued that a direct Phoenix-to-Kingman route would save 100 miles.
evidence.quote: The town of Wickenburg contested that a direct routing between Phoenix and Kingman would be 100 miles (161 km) shorter than the routing through Ash Fork

evidence.claim: The future southern leg entered the state system as SR 93 in 1946.
evidence.quote: On March 23, 1946, what would become the southern leg of US 93 past Kingman was added to the State Highway System as State Route 93.

evidence.claim: The US 93 extension reached US 89 north of Wickenburg in 1965, then continued into Wickenburg in 1992 when US 89 was decommissioned there.
evidence.quote: a southern extension was only accepted by the AASHTO to US 89 north of Wickenburg in 1965.

evidence.claim: then continued into Wickenburg in 1992 when US 89 was decommissioned there.
evidence.quote: Until 1992, US 93 ended a short distance north of Wickenburg, Arizona at a junction with U.S. Route 89. When US 89 was decommissioned in the area, the US 93 designation was carried on into Wickenburg.

evidence.claim: Traveling south from Wikieup, start in the Big Sandy River valley between the Hualapai and Aquarius mountains.
evidence.quote: Wikieup is in southeastern Mohave County in the valley of the Big Sandy River, between the Hualapai Mountains to the west and the Aquarius Mountains to the east.

evidence.claim: US 93 crosses Burro Creek on steel arches and passes Nothing before reaching the Santa Maria River.
evidence.quote: The highway widens to four lanes at the Santa Maria River and continues towards the northwest past a junction with SR 97 on its way to the town of Wikieup. Before reaching that town, it passes the tiny settlement of Nothing (just across the Yavapai – Mohave county line) and crosses Burro Creek over dual steel arch bridges

evidence.claim: The road continues toward the SR 71 junction southwest of Congress, with Wickenburg beyond.
evidence.quote: US 93 continues to the northwest to a junction with SR 71 at a diamond interchange southwest of Congress.

evidence.claim: with Wickenburg beyond.
evidence.quote: The southern terminus of US 93 is located at a junction (rebuilt and relocated between February 2008 and February 2010) with US 60 in Wickenburg

evidence.claim: Two steel arches carry US 93 across Burro Creek, about 400 feet above its intermittent waterway.
evidence.quote: crosses Burro Creek over dual steel arch bridges, which are located about 400 feet (120 metres) above the intermittent waterway.

evidence.claim: The crossing lies between Nothing and Wikieup on the highway through this remote rural country.
evidence.quote: As it continues to the northwest through this scenic but remote rural area, the highway is signed as the Joshua Forest Parkway.

evidence.claim: Farther north, beyond Wikieup, US 93 turns to follow the western edge of the Big Sandy River and Knight Creek toward Interstate 40.
evidence.quote: After passing through Wikieup, US 93 curves north to follow the western edge of the Big Sandy River and one of its tributaries, Knight Creek, on its way toward Interstate 40 (I-40).

evidence.claim: Twin steel arches cross an intermittent waterway.
evidence.quote: crosses Burro Creek over dual steel arch bridges, which are located about 400 feet (120 metres) above the intermittent waterway.

evidence.claim: The crossing lies between Nothing and Wikieup
evidence.quote: Before reaching that town, it passes the tiny settlement of Nothing (just across the Yavapai – Mohave county line) and crosses Burro Creek

evidence.claim: Nothing was a settlement of four people at its height, with a gas station and a small convenience store.
evidence.quote: At its height, Nothing had a population of four. The settlement contained a gas station and small convenience store.

evidence.claim: Richard “Buddy” Kenworthy established it in 1977, 23 miles south of Wikieup on US 93.
evidence.quote: The settlement was established in 1977 by Richard "Buddy" Kenworthy, located 118 miles (190 km) northwest of Phoenix, and 23 miles (37 km) south of Wikieup

evidence.claim: He left by May 2005, and the settlement was abandoned.
evidence.quote: Nothing was abandoned by May 2005 when Kenworthy moved on from the settlement

evidence.claim: A later owner, Mike Jensen, tried a revival, opening a pizza business from a portable oven by April 2009.
evidence.quote: By April 2009, Jensen had opened his pizza business, run from a portable oven

evidence.claim: By April 2011, Nothing was marked as abandoned again.
evidence.quote: In April 2011, Nothing was marked as abandoned once again.

evidence.claim: Joshua trees mark the southern US 93 landscape where the Mohave and Sonoran deserts meet.
evidence.quote: the southern segment runs through a vast array of Joshua trees and the ecological boundaries of the Mohave and Sonoran Deserts.

evidence.claim: In 1993, 54 miles between Wikieup and Wickenburg received recognition as the Joshua Forest Scenic Road for their unusual scenery.
evidence.quote: The unusual scenery along 54 miles of U.S. 93 between Wickieup and Wickenburg earned it recognition as the Joshua Forest Scenic Road in 1993.

evidence.claim: Between 1942 and 1958, crews rebuilt and reworked the highway for the eventual US 93 extension.
evidence.quote: Between 1942 and 1958, the highway was rebuilt and reworked into a suitable highway for an eventual extension of US 93.

evidence.claim: ADOT installed a motorist call box at Nothing, one of four on US 93.
evidence.quote: The Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) installed one of four motorist call boxes on U.S. 93 at Nothing.

flags: The corridor-plan cache (06) is only a Wayback wrapper. It cannot support the former draft’s dense southern forest, yucca size, Mormon naming story, boulder transition, Kaiser Springs views or pollination account. The campground claim is also unsupported and removed.

ADOT supports 54 scenic miles between the named towns but does not give precise scenic endpoints here. The overview distinguishes the larger highway and describes a southbound journey, matching the strip order; no unsupported milepost endpoints are supplied.

All three current moments retained. Their 35–90-word stories are shorter than the target because the subject-specific evidence is limited; Joshua forest was revised to remove repetition. No current stopping access or condition of Nothing’s buildings is established.
